title: Convergent SLO burn-in harness and regional eviction explorer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a repeatable 'burn-in' harness that validates convergent SLO behavior under progressive regional eviction and exercise circuit-breaker boundaries. The harness will drive sequence-aware synthetic traffic (tokenized) while varying admit thresholds, KV-prefetch hitrates, and model-variant fallbacks to surface SLO regressions before rollout. Deliverables: 1) A configurable traffic generator and scenario runner; 2) A Grafana dashboard (explorer) that correlates admit scores, token-level p50/p95/p99, KV-hit ratio, and circuit state transitions; 3) Runbook with failover rehearsal steps and acceptance criteria for canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic harness can replay three canned scenarios (steady-state, microburst, slow-drain) with token-level timing emitted to the observability pipeline
Dashboard shows live correlation between admit_score, p95 token-latency, KV hit ratio and circuit state with <30s ingestion latency
Runbook lists clear thresholds to trigger automated rollback or progressive regional throttle and passes tabletop rehearsal
Two synthetic rehearsals executed in staging with documented findings and follow-ups
PR implementing instrumented metrics and dashboard panels merged and smoke-tested
steps: Design traffic scenarios and tokenization profiles (seq length distribution, prompt prefixes)
Extend synthetic harness to mark request origin region and apply progressive eviction simulation
Instrument additional metrics: admit_score_histogram, kv_prefetch_latency_ms, kv_prefetch_hit_ratio, decode_path_queue_depth
Build Grafana dashboard panels: token latency waterfall, admit heatmap, circuit timeline, regional spillover map
Integrate dashboard with alerting rules for early-warning SLO drift (p95 and error budget burn-rate)
Run two end-to-end rehearsals; capture recordings and issue follow-up tickets for any regressions
decisions: We will use sampled token-level metrics (1 in 20 requests) to limit telemetry cost and a separate synthetic channel for 100% sampling during rehearsals. Circuit state will be recorded as a labeled metric (circuit_state{region,shard}) instead of logs to enable efficient joins in the dashboard. For admit_score, we'll publish both raw and normalized (0-1) versions; alerts should use normalized percentiles.
